activities.anchor: the first lesson in documentary's staged nature
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the founding scandal
activities.name: docNanookSpot

config.prompt: A summary of Nanook of the North contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Nanook of the North (1922) is usually called the first feature documentary.
The walrus hunt was re-enacted for the camera with harpoons the men had stopped using.
The 'wife' in the film was Nanook's actual wife, cast from the community.
The famous igloo interior was built oversized, and cut open, so daylight could reach the film.
Flaherty's reconstructions were, from his point of view, a claim about essence rather than a deception.
config.correction: The 'wife' was not Nanook's wife — the cast was assembled for the camera like any production.
config.why: The audience's trust is a budget the filmmaker spends, and every later school decides differently how much to spend.

activities.anchor: The clearest map of the answers
activities.caption: pair each mode with its truth-claim
activities.name: docModesMatch

config.prompt: Nichols's modes, one sentence each — pair mode with method:

pairs.right: narrates from outside — the voice-of-god commentary and the illustrative image
the fly on the wall — sync-sound, no commentary at all
the filmmaker in the frame and the questions on the track
films documentary itself — the apparatus as protagonist
foregrounds the subjective — lived experience is the evidence

config.why: Knowing which mode a film is in tells you what kind of truth-claim it is licensed to make — half the analytical work before a single shot is read closely.

activities.caption: set the canon in chronological order
activities.name: docCanonOrder

config.prompt: Poetic and expository landmarks — put them in chronological order:
items: Manhatta — Strand and Sheeler's city symphony
Rain — Ivens edits weather as music
The Plow That Broke the Plains — Lorentz's New Deal verse narration
The River — environmental policy argued in verse
Why We Fight — Capra's persuasion-by-montage operation
config.why: From rhythm to newsreel inheritance to wartime persuasion: the poetic line edits as music, the expository line argues — and the war years pushed the second to its peak.

activities.caption: true or false — the objectivity audit
activities.name: docObjectiveJudge

statements.s: Selection is authorship: where the camera stands, when it starts, what ends up on the floor.
statements.why: Every one of those is a choice, and choices are authorship.

statements.s: The accurate claim a documentary can make is 'this is the truth.'
statements.why: The honest claim is 'this is a truth I earned by a method I will show you.'

statements.s: Choosing not to intervene is itself an intervention.
statements.why: Wiseman's silent camera still decides which hour of an institution you will see.
It means 'truth film' — Rouch's participants knew exactly who was provoking them.

activities.anchor: The form's theoretical backbone is a three-way argument
activities.caption: pair each theory with what it argued
activities.name: docTheoryMatch

config.prompt: Three theorists, three theses — pair them:

pairs.right: the machine-eye is superior — film reveals what unaided perception misses
reconstruction in service of a deeper truth about a life before modernity
inform the citizen and justify the form to the state
authority grounded in indexicality — the image is a trace of what was there

config.why: Bruzzi added the twist: documentary is inherently performative — the filming is an event in the world, not a window on it.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — the debates that reopened the question
activities.name: docDebateCloze

config.text: Bazin grounded documentary's authority in %%0%% — the image is a trace of what was there. Stella Bruzzi replied that documentary is inherently %%1%% — the filming is an event in the world. And Roadrunner (2022) disclosed that a handful of spoken words in Anthony Bourdain's mouth were %%2%% — reopening the indexicality question for the synthetic age.
config.hint: When images can be generated, 'it happened on camera' is no longer self-certifying.

activities.caption: call the runtime — the testimony marathon
activities.name: docShoahEstimate

config.prompt: Claude Lanzmann's Shoah (1985) uses no archival footage — only testimony. Roughly how long does it run?
config.why: Nine and a half hours of testimony — the film that reset the evidentiary standard for how atrocity can be represented at all.
config.context: No archival footage, no reconstruction: witness voices carry the whole evidentiary load.

activities.anchor: The serious evaluative question borrows from the policy lesson
activities.caption: the commissioning board — what counts as impact?
activities.name: docImpactBranch

config.root: Your documentary premiered: festival buzz, a streaming deal, trending for a week. The board asks: did it matter?

start.text: What do you bring to the meeting as evidence?

choices.label: Box office and viewing figures
choices.feedback: The audience count — and what does it count?

choices.label: Awards and viral spread
choices.feedback: The same trap with better lighting.

choices.label: What behaviour, law or institution was different afterwards

attention.text: Attention is not change, and attention fades. The Thin Blue Line is counted differently: its demonstration that Randall Dale Adams was innocent helped free him the following year — an outcome, not a gross.

spread.text: An Inconvenient Truth took the Oscar and is credited with moving climate change to dinner-table politics — but the credit rests on what happened afterwards, not on the statuette.

evidence.text: Blackfish contributed to SeaWorld ending its orca breeding programme in 2016; Shoah reset the evidentiary standard for representing atrocity — documentable shifts, each with a chain of evidence back to the film.

config.why: What was different afterwards, and what evidence connects the film to it — impact is the hardest thing to claim honestly.
